pr_title: Don't detect PlainActionFuture deadlock on concurrent complete
pr_body:
Closes #110360
Closes #110181 

I don't love the test for this, but it does reproduce the issue reliably. Any suggestions for making it less verbose are appreciated.

comments:
~This is the same cause as [this issue](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/109792). It's because `org.elasticsearch.action.support.PlainActionFuture#assertCompleteAllowed` only takes into account the executor name, and not the node & executor name when determining if we're risking a deadlock.~

No it's not, it's genuinely the same executor. Taking a look.

[This build scan](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/7tm7ijw3ijumg/tests/task/:modules:reindex:test/details/org.elasticsearch.reindex.AsyncBulkByScrollActionTests/testScrollResponseBatchingBehavior?expanded-stacktrace=WyIwIl0&top-execution=1) is more illustrative of the problem I believe, it looks like two threads are attempting to complete/fail the `PlainActionFuture` concurrently. I assume the first one in would usually do its thing and the second one would be prevented from doing so, but because of the safety check (which is necessarily done without acquiring the mutex) it fails? I will keep digging.

This appears to be an issue with threads concurrently resolving the `PlainActionFuture`.

It happens when multiple threads call `complete` simultaneously
- one thread successfully calls `compareAndSet(RUNNING, COMPLETING)` and proceeds to set the value/exception
- a second thread fails `compareAndSet(RUNNING, COMPLETING)` while the state is still `COMPLETING` so it calls `acquireShared` to wait for the first thread to finish its call to `complete`.
- a third thread from the same pool as the second thread calls `assertCompleteAllowed` which throws because there is a thread from the same pool waiting on the result.

This explains the strange stack traces that don't appear to show the waiter waiting on the `PlainActionFuture` (it has usually moved on by the time the stack trace is printed).

This is technically not a false-positive because there is genuinely a thread from the same pool waiting for the result of the future, but the reason its waiting means it is a false positive (because the waiter will not be blocked indefinitely).

I've been able to reproduce this with only two threads provided they are in a tight loop calling `onFailure`/`onResult` so we don't strictly need three threads for this to occur (in the two-thread case, the thread that succeeds in completing the future comes back and calls complete again while the waiting thread is still waiting).

Why this scenario arises in this test I'm not sure, both the threads seem to be calling onFailure, but the deadlock detection causes the original exception to be swallowed.

review_comments: I imagine we stay in this state extremely briefly (and rarely) as we're just waiting on two assignments and the release, perhaps busy wait is OK here?
We could also use some other synchronisation mechanism here to wait/notify (that didn't add the waiter to the waiters for the `Sync`), but that might be overkill?
Seems ok to me; possibly this is even more efficient, not that efficiency particularly matters in these cases.
Seems fine to me as well. I think `acquire` internally also does busy waiting.
Would it help to wait on the future to be completed too?

I actually don't think so, I tried replacing the sleep with a wait and that made the test unreliable. I measured, and on my machine each thread completed that loop about 800,000 times in the ~20ms so I feel waiting on the future (in addition to the sleep) is at best redundant and at worst interfering with the behaviour under test.
